## Strings and operators {#strings .terminal-demo}

```python
print("combine" + "these" + "together")
print("combine" + " " + "these" + " " + "together")
print("time: " + str(3) + " o'clock")
print("SPAM" * 3)
message = "I am a computer"
print(len(message))
print(type(len(message)))
```

`+` joins strings. `*` repeats a string an integer number of times.

`len()` gives the length. A string can contain letters, digits, spaces and Unicode characters.

## String methods {#string-methods .ide-demo}


```python
message = " ada Lovelace "
print(message.upper())
print(message.lower())
print(message.title())
print(repr(message.strip()))
print(message.split(" "))
print(" ".join(message.split()))
```

Methods can be chained: the next method acts on the value returned by the previous one. `strip()` removes outside whitespace; `join()` joins pieces of text.

## Positions and slices {#indexing .keep-code .index-slide}

| Character | `P` | `Y` | `T` | `H` | `O` | `N` |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Index | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| Negative index | −6 | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 |

```python
s = "PYTHON"
print(s[0])      # 'P'
print(s[-2])     # 'O'
print(s[0:3])    # 'PYT'
```

**`s[start:stop:step]`** includes start, excludes stop and defaults to a step of `1`.

## Strings are immutable {#immutable .ide-demo}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
An item assignment raises an error:

```python
message = "ada Lovelace"
message[0] = "A"
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Reassignment uses a new string value:

```python
message = "ada Lovelace"
message = "A" + message[1:]
print(message)
```
:::
::::

An item assignment cannot change the string. Reassignment binds the name to a new string value.

## How do I remove the outside spaces and format the name properly in the fewest steps? {#format-name .ide-demo}

```python
name = " ada loveLACE "
name = name.strip().title()
print(name)
```

Chaining the methods keeps the transformation in one expression.

The result is `Ada Lovelace`. Assign it if you want `name` to refer to the formatted value.

## Robot Lab: extracting the distance {#robot-distance .robot-demo}

The detector supplies a **string** such as `"  d:080  "`.

How do we extract the distance as an `int` and set it to `distance_cm`?

```{.python .robot-python}
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])
print(distance_cm)
print(type(distance_cm))
```

## One conditional block {#one-if .ide-demo .with-robot}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
**VS Code/IDE**

```python
distance_cm = 80
if distance_cm > 20:
    print("FORWARD")
print("Reading checked")
```
:::
::: {.column width="53%"}
**Robot Lab**

```{.python .robot-python}
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])
if distance_cm > 20:
    print("FORWARD")
print("Reading checked")
```
:::
::::

The condition produces `True` or `False`. A **colon** starts the block. **Four spaces** show what belongs inside it.

[Then Robot Lab](https://josephpb.github.io/2026-sdpa/additional_materials/robot-lab/){.robot-link .demo-link target="robot-lab"} · Keep hitting Run as the reading changes. At 20 cm, no FORWARD instruction runs.

## A chain chooses at most one branch {#elif-chain .ide-demo}

```python
raw = "  d:080  "
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])
if distance_cm <= 20:
    print("STOP")
elif distance_cm <= 50:
    print("SLOW")
else:
    print("FORWARD")
print("Reading checked")
```

Python takes the **first true branch**. How would you rewrite this to print both `STOP` and `SLOW` when the distance is 20 cm?

## Multiple `if` statements {#independent-if .keep-code}

```{.python}
distance_cm = 20
if distance_cm <= 20:
    print("STOP")
if distance_cm <= 50:
    print("SLOW")
print("Done")
```

**A** `STOP, Done`  **B** `SLOW, Done`  **C** `STOP, SLOW, Done`

::: {.answer}
**C.** Each `if` starts a separate decision. Indentation decides which statements belong to a block.
:::

## Nested decisions {#nested-decisions .ide-demo}

```python
distance_cm = 80

if distance_cm <= 100:
    if distance_cm > 20:
        print("FORWARD")
    else:
        print("STOP")
else:
    print("PAUSE")
```

`if distance_cm <= 100 and distance_cm > 20:` combines the tests for moving.

## `while` loop {#while-loop .ide-demo .with-robot}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="43%"}
**VS Code/IDE**

```python
distance_cm = 80
while distance_cm > 20:
    print("FORWARD")
    distance_cm -= 20
print("STOP")
```
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Robot Lab**

```{.python .robot-python}
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])
while distance_cm > 20:
    print("FORWARD")
    message = raw.strip()
    distance_cm = int(message[2:])
print("STOP")
```
:::
::::

The IDE example changes a simulated distance. In Robot Lab, re-read the detector after moving.

[Then Robot Lab](https://josephpb.github.io/2026-sdpa/additional_materials/robot-lab/){.robot-link .demo-link target="robot-lab"} · Reset to 80 cm, run, then try starting at 20 cm.

## A stale reading {#stale-reading .keep-code}

```{.python}
raw = " d:080 "
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])

while distance_cm > 20:
    print("FORWARD")
```

What happens next? **A** Stops at 20  **B** Keeps printing FORWARD  **C** Does not print

::: {.answer}
**B.** `distance_cm` still contains `80`. In Robot Lab, read and convert the supplied `raw` after each move; do not overwrite it with a fixed string.
:::

::: {.student-only .small}
This deliberately nonterminating example can be interrupted with Stop. The slide runner also limits excessive output.
:::

## Repetition with keyboard input {#input-loop .ide-demo}

A robot asks for a turn until you type `left`.

```python
turn = input("Turn left or right? ").strip().lower()
while turn != "left":
    turn = input("Turn left or right? ").strip().lower()
print("Route confirmed")
```

What happens for `right`, `RIGHT`, `alpaca`, then `left`?

## `for` loops and `range` {#for-sequence .ide-demo}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
**Iterating through a string**

```python
route = "FFPFSFF"
for instruction in route:
    print(instruction)
```

Each iteration visits the next character. No manual counter is needed.
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
**Iterating through integers**

```python
for attempt in range(3):
    print("Reading", attempt)
for n in range(5, 40, 10):
    print(n)
for n in range(40, 5, -10):
    print(n)
```
:::
::::

Start included. Stop excluded. The defaults are **start `0`** and **step `1`**.

## Reassigning the variable in the loop {#fixed-range .keep-code}

```{.python}
x = 4
for i in range(x):
    print(i)
    x = 5
```

**A** `0, 1, 2, 3`  **B** `0, 1, 2, 3, 4`  **C** Never finishes

::: {.answer}
**A.** Changing `x` does not rebuild the existing range for this loop.
:::

## `break` and `continue` {#route-control .ide-demo}

```python
route = "FFPFSFF"
for instruction in route:
    if instruction == "S":
        print("STOP")
        break
    if instruction == "P":
        print("PAUSE")
        continue
    print("FORWARD")
```

`break` exits this loop. `continue` skips to its next iteration.

## Robot Lab: a route string {#robot-route .robot-demo}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
Reset to **80 cm**. Build a `for` loop for `"FFPFSFF"`.

**F** means FORWARD.
**S** means STOP and `break`.
**P** means PAUSE and `continue`.

Final distance: **A** 0  **B** 20  **C** 40  **D** 60 cm

::: {.answer}
**B.** Three moves, one pause, then STOP. The final two `F`s are skipped.
:::

[Open Robot Lab](https://josephpb.github.io/2026-sdpa/additional_materials/robot-lab/){.robot-link .demo-link target="robot-lab"}
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
```{.python .robot-python}
message = raw.strip()
distance_cm = int(message[2:])
for instruction in "FFPFSFF":
    if instruction == "S":
        print("STOP")
        break
    if instruction == "P":
        print("PAUSE")
        continue
    print("FORWARD")
    message = raw.strip()
    distance_cm = int(message[2:])
```
:::
::::

## `break` in the innermost loop {#nested-break .ide-demo}

```python
for trial in range(2):
    for instruction in "FSF":
        if instruction == "S":
            break
    print("Trial finished", trial)
```

How many times does the final `print` run?

**Twice.** The outer loop continues after the inner loop ends.

## Reference: string methods {#strings-reference .keep-code}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```python
s = "  ada LOVELACE  "
print(s.upper())
print(s.lower())
print(s.title())
print(repr(s.lstrip()))
print(repr(s.rstrip()))
print(repr(s.strip()))
print(len(s))
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```python
s = "PYTHON"
print(s[:3])
print(s[3:])
print(s[::2])
print(s[::-1])
print(str(80), int("080"))
```
:::
::::

Strings are immutable. Methods return values; assignment chooses what a name refers to. `len()` counts Unicode code points, which need not equal the number of visible symbols.

## Reference: looping approaches {#loop-reference .keep-code}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="32%"}
**Characters directly**

```python
s = "FFPFSFF"
for ch in s:
    print(ch)
```
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
**Positions from `range`**

```python
s = "FFPFSFF"
for i in range(len(s)):
    print(i, s[i])
```
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
**A `while` counter**

```python
s = "FFPFSFF"
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    print(i, s[i])
    i += 1
```
:::
::::

Direct iteration is usually clearest when only the character matters. A `while` counter needs an explicit update.
